claims.statement: The phase 1 migration plan splits the Squarespace import into extract, transform, media, load and a review queue for pages with oddities.

dom.ts parses Squarespace HTML with a shared happy-dom Window that disables JavaScript evaluation, script, CSS and iframe loading, computed style rendering and all navigation, and releaseDom closes that window so the next parse opens a fresh one.
normalizedText returns a node's text with all whitespace, including non-breaking spaces, collapsed to single spaces and trimmed.
happy-dom is pinned by a security override and is also a direct dev dependency at the same version because the import parses untrusted Squarespace HTML with it.
parsePage takes the page title from the collection title in the context JSON Squarespace embeds, returning null when it is missing or its escapes are not valid JSON.

parsePage orders the blocks of each fluid-engine section by desktop grid row and then column, preferring the rule inside @media (min-width: 768px) over the mobile rule, puts blocks without a position last, and keeps sections in page order.

Text blocks are parsed into their top-level elements with tag, outer HTML and normalized text; image blocks keep the data-image or data-src URL without its query string and the trimmed alt; embed blocks become https video URLs, unwrapping Embedly, and an embed whose URL does not end up as https, such as javascript: or data: even inside Embedly, becomes an unknown block; other types become unknown blocks.
toQuestGuide never throws on page content; what does not fit is collected in oddities for review in the panel.
The guide title is the Squarespace page title, falling back to the leading heading and then the slug, and originalUrl is https://www.torrentearcano.com/ followed by the slug.

Only an H1 or H2 that is the very first element of the page, with no earlier text element or other block, is dropped as the title heading; every later heading is body content. When the page has a title that differs from the dropped heading after ignoring accents, case, punctuation and a leading number, an oddity keeps the heading's full text.

Lines starting with Prerrequisitos, Necesitarás or Recompensas followed by a colon, compared without accents or case and checked first so a label sent as a heading still counts, fill the matching summary field (for Necesitarás, its notes) with the rest of the line and the following elements of the same text block, headings included, one line per list item, joined by newlines, and stay out of the body; without the colon the line is prose.

A

paragraph starting with the closing sentence Aquí termina la misión loses only that sentence, which can end at . ! ? or an ellipsis; the rest of the paragraph stays, a paragraph with nothing else is dropped, and lists and headings with those words stay whole.

The first

paragraph starting with Habla con X [x,y] (only when its sentence says para empezar) or La misión empieza hablando con X [x,y] fills startNpc without a leading article, startX and startY; a start line in a list or heading does not count.
A bare start sentence is removed from the body while the rest of its paragraph is kept with its formatting; a start line with more information stays whole in the body.

Paragraphs starting with all-caps IMPORTANTE, CUIDADO or ATENCIÓN become warning callouts and NOTA becomes a tip callout, including what is left of a trimmed paragraph; a label followed by a colon or exclamation mark is removed and the rest starts with a capital letter.

Consecutive prose elements of one Squarespace text block are joined into one richText block that keeps HTML until the loader converts it to Lexical; images become image blocks with the guide title as fallback alt, videos become video blocks, and unknown blocks are left out of the body.

Oddities record an invalid slug, a missing page title, a missing DofusDB quest, each missing summary block (including a label with no text), a missing start line, a body that could not be split into steps, each unknown Squarespace block and a dropped title heading that differs from the page title.
createHtmlToLexical builds the editor config from Payload's sanitized config and runs convertHTMLToLexical with a happy-dom wrapper shaped like JSDOM.

parseQuestMatches reads quest_matches.csv from the migration inventory into a map from slug to space-separated DofusDB quest IDs and an ambiguous flag set when the column is True, handling quoted fields and a leading BOM, and throws when the slug, quest_ids or ambiguous column is missing.
GUIDE_SLUGS lists the five guides of the first import: el-cazador-cazado, intoxicacion-profunda, operacion-envenenamiento, entretanto-un-renacer and seis-pies-bajo-tierra.
The import unit tests run on trimmed Squarespace pages in tests/fixtures/squarespace/, which Prettier ignores so the parser reads them as saved.
The Lexical state returned by createHtmlToLexical is typed as a richText block's content from the generated Payload types.
loadQuestGuides is a trusted job that calls the local API with overrideAccess true and takes an injected fetchImage so it can run without network.
When a guide names exactly one DofusDB ID, the loader links the Payload ID of that quest if it is already in the quests collection and records an oddity when the ID is missing from it.

Each image is stored once in media keyed by its original URL: the loader checks a per-run map, then searches media by originalUrl, and only downloads and creates a record with alt and originalUrl when neither has it.
An image that fails to download, whatever its error code, is left out of the body and recorded as an oddity, and the guide still loads.

The loader finds guides by slug including drafts and creates or updates them with title, slug, originalUrl, summary, quest and body, always as drafts, so a published guide stays published until its new draft is published.
A guide whose compared fields equal the stored draft, ignoring IDs and null values, is left untouched so a re-run adds no versions.
A guide with an invalid slug is skipped and counted; the loader returns counts of created, updated, unchanged and skipped guides, created and reused media, and the oddities per slug.
pnpm import:guides runs scripts/import/import-guides.ts with payload run, reads raw/pages/<slug>.html and out/quest_matches.csv from the given inventory folder, and defaults to the five GUIDE_SLUGS.
pnpm import:guides links no quest for an ambiguous match and records the oddity Cruce ambiguo con DofusDB, sin enlazar.
The command prints each oddity and the totals with the elapsed time, and on failure prints an error and exits with code 1 because payload run otherwise exits 0.
The import writes to the DATABASE_URL database, or the pnpm db:dev one when it is empty, and uploads images wherever media storage points.
createImageFetcher refuses, before any request, a URL that does not parse, is not https, is on a host other than images.squarespace-cdn.com or names a port.
The image request does not follow redirects, times out after 30 seconds, and fails on an HTTP error or a response whose content-type is not image/*.

The image request's Accept header names only the type of the file's extension so Squarespace's CDN returns the original instead of WebP, and the file name comes from the URL path with + turned back into spaces.
The loader creates imported media records with alt and originalUrl from the original image, and Payload generates the image sizes on upload.
Agents have full access to dev and read access to prod; prod writes, including database changes, go through release.yml or need Daniel's explicit yes for that one action.

The loader integration test runs on the five fixtures with a fake fetchImage and checks drafts with their blocks and steps, one media record per image with URL and alt, oddities for missing quests, an idempotent second run, one new draft for a changed guide, a summary field that disappears being filled from the linked quest without extra versions on the next run, hidden drafts for anonymous readers, skipping an invalid slug, a guide with several DofusDB IDs saved without a quest, and untitled and marked steps saved with their coordinates.

The loader sends every summary field (prerequisites, rewards, startNpc, startX, startY and needs with its notes and an empty item list) with null for those the conversion did not bring, because Payload keeps group fields an update leaves out; a re-import replaces a removed value once, from DofusDB or with null, and then finds the guide unchanged.
The Squarespace Necesitarás text is converted into summary.needs.notes, leaving the needs item list to DofusDB.

The loader reads linked quests at depth 1 and applies summaryToFill and applySummaryFill with the linked quest before comparing and writing, the same fill the collection hook performs on save, so converted and stored guides compare equal and a rerun saves no version.
When a guide names several distinct DofusDB IDs, the loader links no quest and records the oddity 'Varias misiones de DofusDB (a, b): sin enlazar, elige una en el panel'.

nestSteps splits the converted body into an introduction, step blocks and a closing: by ETAPA n: markers when the page has them, otherwise by units of one text block plus the screenshots that follow it, and leaves the body as prose with an oddity when fewer than two units exist.
Each imported step takes the first [x,y] of its original text, the start line included, as its coordinates, and only a marked step gets a title.

A paragraph starting with all-caps RECOMENDACIÓN or RECOMENDACIONES opens a tip callout that takes the following paragraphs up to its first list, or only a following list when the advice shares the label's paragraph, and a block opening with it continues the previous step.

The loader turns each step into a step block with its title, x and y set to null when absent and its own content blocks, and both the import command and the loader release the shared DOM between guides.

When saving an image fails with a Postgres connection error, detected through SQLSTATE classes 08 and 57P0, socket error codes or connection messages anywhere in the error's cause chain, the loader rethrows and stops instead of recording an image oddity, while fetchImage errors are wrapped in ImageDownloadError so they never count as connection failures.

After a load aborted by a killed Postgres backend, no transaction session remains, neither the image nor the unfinished guide is stored, and the next load creates that guide and its image while leaving the already finished guide unchanged.
The import-disconnect fault-injection fixture refuses non-local database URLs and any database other than ta_web_integration or ta_web, and the test asserts both refusals.
